## 356624: simplified de Bruijn graphs

Exact scope: every word length n>=4 and alphabet size k>=3. The source uses n for LENGTH, not alphabet size. The 17 vertices have length three; that diagram does not supply a length-four witness. Appendix acquired but NOT independently audited through all 100 branching lines.

Route A, induced obstruction lifting. Restricting letters to a subalphabet gives an INDUCED copy of S(n,3) in S(n,k): both overlap equalities are unchanged. Restricting a representing word to a subset of its letters preserves alternation for every remaining pair. Thus non-word-representability is upward closed under induced-supergraph inclusion. This reduces alphabet scope but leaves ALL n>=4. It does not transfer the public n=3 obstruction.

The natural prefix padding fails even as an edge-preserving map. For n=4, the edge 102--021 in S(3,3) maps under prefixing 0 to 0102 and 0021. Their suffix/prefix comparisons are 102 versus 002, and 021 versus 010. Neither agrees. Repeating symbols or inserting separators produces chains of shifts rather than single edges; subdivision is not an authenticated preservation operation for non-word-representability. A periodic-word construction preserves a single cyclic trajectory but does not automatically realize all branches in Figure 2 with consistent histories. The missing lemma is an explicit induced embedding of a non-word-representable obstruction into S(n,3), uniform for n>=4, or a different uniform forbidden-orientation argument. No such embedding is claimed.

Route B, constructing a representation to refute the conjecture. An acyclic orientation is not enough: every directed path of length at least three with adjacent endpoints must span all forward edges. Lexicographic orientation is acyclic but no shortcut-free proof was obtained. A three-coloring would suffice by Petyuk Theorem 2, but the binary proof uses only two final letters and parity of a final run. For three letters, choosing one color for even runs and two for odd runs cannot immediately distinguish all possible one-letter transitions. This is a failed scheme, not an impossibility theorem for three-colorings.

A more promising comparison map assigns to x1...xn its adjacent comparison bits. On words with consecutive unequal letters it maps shifts to binary shifts, but a constant comparison-bit word can occur at multiple distinct vertices (strictly increasing or decreasing words). Their overlap edges collapse to a single loop-removed binary vertex. Therefore a proper binary coloring cannot simply be pulled back. ## 342128: minor-minimal simple matroids

Exact scope is finiteness up to isomorphism of minor-minimal SIMPLE obstructions to covering by k independent sets, for every positive k. Read Campbell–Grace–Oxley–Whittle 1903.05877v1, Introduction, Theorem1.1, Proposition1.2 and proof, Theorem1.3, Lemma1.4 and proof, Conjectures1.5–1.8, Lemma2.1 and proof, and beginning of §3 proof through its wheel/whirl analysis. Later full classification proof and figures not fully audited. The final EJC27(2)P35 was identified by search but remains UNREAD (no denial). Hence source-final gate remains unpaid.

Route A, density and contraction. For a minimal simple obstruction M of rank r with N elements, every proper restriction is k-coverable. By Edmonds, any violating subset must be the entire ground set: N>kr. For any element e, the restriction M\e is coverable; hence N-1<=k r(M\e)<=kr. Thus N=kr+1 and deleting e preserves rank. In particular no coloop. This is the source's own Lemma1.4, independently reconstructed, not a new result.

If r>=2, simplification of M/e is a proper simple minor, hence has at most k(r-1) elements. Consequently contracting e and simplifying loses at least N-k(r-1)=k+1 elements in total, including e. Thus at least k further elements disappear in merging parallel classes. Writing the parallel classes of M/e as C_j, this is sum_j(|C_j|-1)>=k. Pairs within each C_j correspond to triangles through e in the simple original matroid. This imposes local line multiplicity but supplies no uniform upper bound on r. Source Lemma2.1 already gives a density version of this local phenomenon.

Uniform-matroid trial: U_(r,kr+1) is deletion-critical, but if r>=3, contracting an element gives the simple proper minor U_(r-1,kr), which has kr>k(r-1) and remains noncoverable. It therefore fails simple-minor minimality. For r=2 the contraction is rank one with parallel elements, and its simplification has one point; hence U_(2,2k+1) is a legitimate natural obstruction for k>=1 (for k=1 it is the triangle). This is a parameter family within the question, not a refutation of finiteness for fixed k. For k=1, every dependent simple matroid has a circuit of size at least3; contracting circuit elements down to size3 yields U_(2,3), so only the triangle can be minor-minimal. This known elementary endpoint does not settle all k.

Route B, unbounded parallel connections. Parallel-connecting two simple matroids across a common nonloop point has rank r1+r2-1 and size N1+N2-1. The excess N-kr therefore becomes (N1-kr1)+(N2-kr2)+(k-1). Repeating a fixed dense block increases excess for k>=2 rather than maintaining the deletion-critical value 1. In particular glueing already critical excess-one blocks produces excess k+1, contradicting the necessary N=kr+1. One would need blocks with compensating deficits and also prove that every simple contraction becomes coverable; cardinality balance alone is insufficient. Long sparse chains have no authenticated fixed-k minimality argument here. This route is not a constructed infinite antichain.

Route C, well-quasi-order. A minor antichain of minimal obstructions would be finite in any well-quasi-ordered class. But the source itself states this restriction, including representability over a FIXED finite field. The target ranges over arbitrary simple matroids with no fixed field. Varying fields is not a finite union of those classes. There is no unrestricted well-quasi-order input here, and using it would assume the missing structure. No deduction from the announced fixed-field theorem is claimed without its body.

Exact unpaid lemma: a rank bound r<=R(k) for arbitrary minimal simple k-cover obstructions (or an independently justified finite classification mechanism); alternatively a fixed-k unbounded-rank family with full deletion AND simple-contraction minimality. The density equalities, local triangles and k=1,2 cases pay neither alternative. Significance could be high for a full proof; rejection is for the unpaid global bound, not shortness or standard-tool usage.

## 381465: finite groups and multiple full-length product-one blocks

Use the source's exact nonabelian convention: subsequences are multisets of POSITIONS, and the chosen terms may be reordered so their product is identity. An order-preserving product condition would be a different question. Theorem7.2, its proof, Corollary7.3 and Conjecture7.4 in Zakarczemny1905.07648v2 read in full. Relevant introductory definitions also read. m is positive. The trivial group has d=0 and E_m=m, so is harmless and is not a creditable endpoint correction.

Route A, full m reduction. Let N=|G| and take a product-one-free sequence A of maximal length d. It contains no identity. Append mN-1 identities. A product-one subsequence containing any terms of A would, after removing identities from its ordering, give a nonempty product-one subsequence of A. Therefore every product-one block uses identities only. There are too few identities for m disjoint N-blocks; hence E_m>=d+mN. For the upper bound, start with E(G)+(m-1)N terms. Remove one N-term product-one subsequence by the definition of E(G). The remaining sequence has length E(G)+(m-2)N, so induction gives all m disjoint blocks. This proves E_m<=E(G)+(m-1)N. Thus E(G)=d+N implies the full m assertion; the converse follows on setting m=1. This is EXACTLY the existing Theorem7.2 reduction, not a new solution or separate family credit.

Route B, lifting via a quotient. If H is normal, one can extract |G:H|-term blocks whose quotient products are identity, producing terms in H. Their internal orderings must be retained when multiplying block products; simply treating unordered noncommuting quotient lifts as sums is invalid. The October2026 source Lemma2.10 proves E(G)<=q(E(H)-1)+E(G/H), q=|G:H|, by extracting E(H) quotient blocks and then |H| product-one block products. This is a valid coarse upper bound. Substituting inductive equalities gives N+q d(H)+d(G/H). The usual concatenation lower bound has direction d(G)>=d(H)+d(G/H), which is far too weak to replace q d(H) by d(G). An induction that silently makes that replacement is invalid. A new sharp extraction principle tied to d(G), not just E(H), is unpaid. For simple groups there is no useful proper normal quotient, so such an induction alone cannot cover all groups anyway.

Route C, strongest current bound. Qu2610.26122v1 (19 October2026) §1 Conjecture1.3, Theorem1.4, Corollary1.5 and §§2.1–2.2 definitions and proofs through Lemma2.10 read. For no cyclic subgroup of smallest-prime index, it gives E(G)<=N+N/p-1, while d(G)<=N/p-1. These are TWO UPPER bounds, not an equality bridge.
